research_scope: Four reviewed aliases into three distinct module/set constructions: finite free left R-module, set-surjectivity, generated submodule. No identity by lexical similarity.

aliases.reason: All occurrences are the finite free left R-module R^n, the direct sum of finitely many copies of the regular module, where m and n are arbitrary finite rank parameters. The scope includes n=0. A finitely generated module need not be free, and a locally free module need not be globally free. Full source-context review confirms phrase 'finite free module R^n' is the same candidate as 'finite rank free module R^n'; keep source wording intact.

All occurrences are the finite free left R-module R^n, the direct sum of finitely many copies of the regular module, where m and n are arbitrary finite rank parameters. The scope includes n=0. A finitely generated module need not be free, and a locally free module need not be globally free. Full source-context review confirms phrase 'R^m and R^n' is the same candidate as 'finite rank free module R^n'; keep source wording intact.

Both references require onto-ness of the underlying function of an R-linear map from a free module to M; that is ordinary surjectivity. R-linearity and the free domain are separately preserved, so the general set-theoretic predicate is the common prerequisite. Full source-context review confirms phrase 'surjective module homomorphism R^n→M' is the same candidate as 'surjective R-linear map R^n→M'; keep source wording intact.

The source occurrences denote the R-submodule of M generated by chosen elements, i.e. finite R-linear combinations. A list generating the entire module is the additional equality of this span with M, not a different meaning of span. Full source-context review confirms phrase 'finite generated submodule sum Rm_1+⋯+Rm_n' is the same candidate as 'R-linear span of generators m_1,…,m_n'; keep source wording intact.
